You are V-MO, the motion design and assembly session for the Heirloom demo video. Read ~/brief/VIDEO-BRIEF.md fully. Load the data from `site/web/public/site.json` and evals. Install ffmpeg if missing (`sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg`). Confirm `npx remotion still` renders a test frame and **Read it**.
2. (≤45 min) The components from the brief: `KineticTitle`, `BrassUnderline`, `GuillocheRing`, `Hallmark`, `DistroPlates`, `CveCascade`, `DatePlates`, `Terminal` (real lines), `VerdictChip`, `CalibrationTriangle`, `GateChecklist`, `LowerThird`, `Counter`, `BacktestSplit`, `PrecedentSeal`, `CaptureClip`, `IrisTransition`, `EndCard`, `Captions`.
   - Build the 10 scenes S01–S10 per the timeline. Where a capture isn't ready yet, use a labelled placeholder frame that the real clip replaces later.
   - Render a still at the key moment of each scene, **Read every still**, write the critique in `video/NOTES.md` and improve. At least two passes on S01–S05: the first 45 s decide everything.
3. (≤10 min) `video/timing.json` + `video/scripts/retime.mjs` (ffprobe the VO files in `video/public/audio/vo/S01.mp3…S10.mp3` when present; pad 0.4 s head and 0.6 s tail; S10 holds the end card 4 s) and caption generation (`.srt` + burned-in style).
   Support the optional `music.mp3` (−18 dB, ducked to −24 dB under VO) and `sfx/*.mp3` cues. Write a SFX cue list with timecodes into the edit guide.
4. (≤25 min) Integrate the captures. Poll `~/video-out/captures/manifest.json` every 60 s (meanwhile keep polishing scenes).
   - Copy or symlink the clips into `video/public/captures/` and replace the placeholders.
   - Give capture clips a subtle cinematic treatment: 2–4% slow push-in, a soft vignette, and a thin brass frame or rounded window when composited over ink.
   - If captures are still missing at minute 95, render with what exists and list the gaps.
5. (≤20 min) Render to `~/video-out/`:
   - `master/HeirloomDemo-silent.mp4` (1080p60, H.264 CRF 14), `master/HeirloomDemo-captions.mp4` (burned captions), `master/HeirloomDemo.srt`;
   - `scenes/S01.mp4…S10.mp4`;
   - `stills/` (one keyframe per scene);
   - if `video/public/audio/vo/*.mp3` exist, also `master/HeirloomDemo-mix.mp4`.
   Use `--concurrency` to use the 8 cores. Extract 1 frame per 2 s from the master and **Read a sample of 12** (the first 45 s especially). Fix anything ugly, then re-render.
6. Write `~/video-out/EDIT-GUIDE.md`:
   - scene timecodes and VO file placement;
   - SFX cues with timecodes and ElevenLabs SFX prompts;
   - music placement and levels;
   - the neatlogs slot (where the owner drops a 6 s recording of a trace);
   - export settings for YouTube (1080p60, H.264 16–20 Mbps, AAC 320 kbps);
   - the upload title, description and chapters.

Rules:
- Every number from data.
- Only the brief's VO text in captions.
- "Candidate backports"; the exact Ubuntu claim sentence; no exploitability claim.
- Never print .env values.

Finish with the output file list (sizes and durations), the scene timecodes, and what still needs the owner.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a live pane or panel, a band above the prompt, a status line, a toast, a slash command, or a hook on tool calls or prompts. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.
- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. # Heirloom demo video: production brief

**Goal:** a ≤2:50 product-launch-quality demo film for Heirloom (an agent that keeps end-of-life software patched). Viewers decide in the first 45 s.
- The owner supplies the voiceover (ElevenLabs), and possibly music and SFX, and does the final mix.
- We supply everything visual: real screen captures (frame-perfect), motion design, a picture-locked master timed to the script, per-scene clips, captions and an edit guide.

## Look and feel
- **Same world as the site** (https://heirloom-proof.vercel.app): "Proof instrument". Ink `#08090A`, raised `#0F1112`/`#16191B`, line `#23272A`, bone `#ECE6DA`, muted `#9A958A`, brass `#C8A86A`/`#E6CB8E`/`#8A6F3E`.
- **Verdict colours:** FIX READY `#5BC98F`, NOT AFFECTED `#7FB2FF`, UNPROVEN `#E8B44C`, AFFECTED `#FF6B5E`, NO PROBE `#8D8A83`.
- **Type:** Instrument Serif (display, italic accents), Geist (UI), Geist Mono (ids, hashes, terminal). The font files are in `site/web/public/fonts` or fontsource.
- **Motion language:** precise, confident, clockwork.
  - Eases `cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1)` (out) and `(0.65,0,0.35,1)` (in-out).
  - Springs `{damping: 200}` for UI, slightly bouncier `{damping: 18, stiffness: 120}` for stamps.
  - Kinetic type reveals word by word (y 24 px → 0, opacity, 40 ms stagger).
  - Guilloché lines draw on (stroke-dashoffset). Brass hairline underlines grow from the left.
  - Transitions: cuts on beat, a brass-ring iris or a gear-tooth wipe at act breaks.
- **No:** cheesy glitch, lens flares, purple, stock "hacker" footage, fake UI.
- Everything shown must be **real** (real site, real GitHub pages, real command output, real data from `site/web/public/site.json` and `evals/*.json`). Never fake the neatlogs UI: leave a labelled slot for the owner's recording.
- **Format:** 1920×1080, **60 fps**, H.264 High, yuv420p, Rec.709. Masters at CRF 14 (preset slow). A YouTube copy at about 16 Mbps. Silent renders; audio is optional (see Audio).

## Timeline (target 2:45; the VO is the spine; durations are re-timed to the real VO files when they arrive)
| # | Time | VO (exact text the owner will generate) | Visuals |
|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | 0:00–0:09 | "On the seventh of April, Django four-point-two reached end of life. No more security fixes." | Black → macro watch-movement b-roll (stock, or our 3D render), a single tick. Kinetic serif "7 April 2026" → "Django 4.2 · end of life", with a brass underline drawing. |
| S02 | 0:09–0:21 | "But Debian thirteen and Ubuntu twenty-four-oh-four still ship it. Since then, Django has published nineteen security advisories — and not one official patch for four-point-two." | Two engraved brass plates slide in: "Debian 13 · python-django 3:4.2.28-0+deb13u2" and "Ubuntu 24.04 · 3:4.2.11-1ubuntu1.18" (real strings). Then 19 real CVE ids cascade into a column, each getting a red "NO 4.2 PATCH" stamp, and the counter lands on "19 advisories · 0 upstream 4.2 patches". |
| S03 | 0:21–0:41 | "On October first, Ubuntu shipped a backport for one of them. Five days later, Django said its original fix was incomplete. We took Ubuntu's source package, ran a test calibrated on Django's own fix commits… and the code path Django closed is still reachable in Ubuntu's build." | Date plates "Oct 1 · Ubuntu ships its CVE-2026-15307 backport" and "Oct 6 · Django: CVE-2026-87890 amends that fix" lock around a glowing "5 days" band. Terminal (Geist Mono) shows the REAL probe run lines from the noble logs (FAIL ×3, `AssertionError: Lists differ: [<class 'bytes'>, <class 'bytes'>] != []`) → verdict chip AFFECTED → the claim sentence in serif: "noble's CVE-2026-15307 backport leaves the bytes path that upstream closed as CVE-2026-87890; our calibrated probe shows it." Small caption: "hand-written probe, calibrated on Django's fix commits dd0558d1^ / dd0558d1". |
| S04 | 0:41–0:52 | "That test was run by Heirloom — an agent that keeps end-of-life software patched, and proves which old versions are actually vulnerable." | Logo reveal: 3D brass movement (our render) turning. The hallmark seal stamps in; wordmark "Heirloom"; tagline "Old software, *kept honest.*" Cut to the site hero (capture). |
| S05 | 0:52–1:11 | "Its first rule: never trust a test that hasn't failed. For each advisory, Heirloom writes its own test, proves it fails on Django's vulnerable code and passes on the fix… and only then asks the real question: is the old version affected?" | Giant kinetic serif: "Never trust a test that hasn't failed." Then the **calibration triangle** motion graphic: U⁻ "upstream before fix" → 3 red FAIL lights; U⁺ "after fix" → 3 green PASS lights; then the line "Django 4.2.30" → verdict chip. Gates C1–C4 tick on. Cut to the site register → receipt certificate opening (capture). |
| S06 | 1:11–1:39 | "Then we let it run the whole campaign: nineteen advisories, replayed in the order Django published them. Thirteen candidate backports — each one failing before the fix, and passing after. Where it couldn't prove something, it filed the evidence instead of guessing. And when a new fix amended one it had already backported, it stacked the follow-up on its own pull request." | Site "Watch it work" capture: the bezel dial turning, tiles stamping in. Overlay lower-thirds: "13 candidate backports · FAIL×3 → PASS×3", "5 unproven → evidence filed, not guessed", "Oct 6 · stacked on its own backport · PR #21 on #20". A quick montage of the GitHub PR list (13 PRs) and PR #21's "Stacked on #20". |
| S07 | 1:39–1:56 | "Across the whole campaign, it asked me one question — a real judgement call about changing Django's behaviour. I answered once. It sealed the answer as a precedent, and the next case reused it without asking." | Site question-thread capture → GitHub issue #6 (the question + the owner's `/heirloom answer adopt-upstream-tests` comment) → the "PRECEDENT SEALED P001" stamp → PR #19 citing P001. |
| S08 | 1:56–2:19 | "We tested the method on cases with known answers. A naive pipeline once called a vulnerable version safe. Heirloom: zero times. Every claim in every pull request links to its neat-logs trace, and every backport links the Entire session of the agent that wrote it." | A backtest split motion graphic: "Naive pipeline: 1 false 'not affected'" (red) vs "Heirloom: 0" (green), with real numbers from evals/results.json. Then GitHub PR #13's claims table (capture) → **[SLOT: owner's neatlogs trace recording, 6 s]** → the PR commit's `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer (capture) → a terminal typing the real `entire checkpoint explain` output (from docs/entire/checkpoint-pr13-*.txt). |
| S09 | 2:19–2:30 | "Each advisory cost about twenty cents of model time. We modelled the business in C-F-O dot A-I: what that's worth to the teams who keep old software alive." | Count-up "$0.22 model cost per advisory (measured)" (from data) → site economics cards → the cfo.ai Base page (capture). |
| S10 | 2:30–2:45 | "Heirloom. Old software, kept honest. Every verdict is a test run you can open." | The site finale (the movement slowing to a stop) → end card: hallmark, "Heirloom", "heirloom-proof.vercel.app", "github.com/iamdflame/heirloom", "Built during #neatHack with neatlogs · Entire · cfo.ai". |

**Captions:** burned-in subtitles of the VO (Geist 34 px, bone on a 70% ink pill, bottom-centre, ≤42 chars per line), plus an `.srt`. Many viewers watch muted on X.

## Captures (session V-CAP): frame-perfect, 60 fps
- **Method (virtual time):** Playwright + Chromium, viewport 1920×1080. `page.clock.install()` before load; per frame, `page.clock.runFor(1000/60)`, set the scroll position, then screenshot (JPEG q=92) → `ffmpeg -framerate 60` → MP4 (CRF 14).
  - This gives perfectly smooth 60 fps even though the box renders WebGL slowly.
  - First verify that the fake clock drives Motion and three.js (two frames 1 s apart must differ). If it doesn't, use CDP `Emulation.setVirtualTimePolicy`.
  - Scroll with easing (in-out) between keyframe positions. Use a local `vite preview` of main's build with a `?capture=1` flag (disables Lenis and exposes `window.__scrollTo`) if needed. Also check that the result matches production.
- **Shots** (file names `~/video-out/captures/<ID>.mp4`):
  - **SH01** hero idle (3D movement turning), 8 s.
  - **SH02** hero → scroll to "Watch it work", 4 s.
  - **SH03** the full "Watch it work" campaign, 16 s (dial, stamps, the Oct 6 connector).
  - **SH04** finding section (plates lock, terminal FAIL×3), 9 s.
  - **SH05** register → a visible cursor moves to CVE-2026-6907 × Django 4.2.30 → click → receipt certificate with the calibration triangle animating, 10 s.
  - **SH06** method gear train, 8 s.
  - **SH07** question thread, 9 s.
  - **SH08** proof numbers, 6 s.
  - **SH09** economics, 6 s.
  - **SH10** evidence locker, 6 s.
  - **SH11** finale, 9 s.
  - **SHM** mobile 390×844 at DSF 3 scrolling the hero and campaign, 8 s.
- **Cursor:** render a tasteful custom cursor (a bone-coloured dot with a ring) injected into the page, moving on eased paths. No OS cursor.
- **GitHub** (dark colour scheme, logged out):
  - **GH01** PR #13: title, verdict table, then a smooth scroll to the claims table, 10 s.
  - **GH02** issue #6: the question → the owner's answer comment, 9 s.
  - **GH03** PR #19: the P001 citation, 6 s.
  - **GH04** PR #21: "Stacked on #20", 5 s.
  - **GH05** a backport commit page showing the `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer, 5 s.
  - **GH06** the fork's PR list (13 candidate backports), 5 s.
  - Hide cookie banners; zoom 125% so the text is legible in 1080p.
- **Other:** **CFO01** the cfo.ai Base Page (https://app.cfo.ai/s/25vRDQClPxqPWB5g), 8 s, if it renders headless. **EOL01** endoflife.date/django, 4 s.
- **3D beauty renders** (from the site's three demo, virtual time; a small `?shot=` camera-path param is fine):
  - **R3D01** a slow orbit around the movement, 10 s.
  - **R3D02** a macro dolly onto the "H" medallion, 6 s.
  - **R3D03** the gears speeding up, 5 s.
- **Stock b-roll:** 2–4 clips from **Pexels** (Pexels License) or **Mixkit** (Mixkit License) only. Macro mechanical watch movement or escapement ticking; brass gears turning. 1080p or higher. Record source URL and licence in `video/ASSETS.md`. Trim to the best 6–10 s and colour-match to ink/brass (ffmpeg `eq`/`curves`, slight desaturation).
- Write `~/video-out/captures/manifest.json` (id, file, duration, fps, source).

## Motion design and assembly (session V-MO): Remotion
- **Project:** `video/` in the heirloom repo (Remotion 4, TS, React). Renders are git-ignored; outputs go to `~/video-out/`.
- **Data:** import `site/web/public/site.json` (or `src/data/site.json`) and read evals for every number. Terminal lines come from real files: the noble 87890 probe logs on the `artifacts` branch (`git show artifacts:matrix/b4-20261011/CVE-2026-87890/...`), and `docs/entire/checkpoint-pr13-*.txt`.
- **Components:**
  - `KineticTitle`, `BrassUnderline`, `GuillocheRing` (procedural; reuse the site's generator), `Hallmark`;
  - `DistroPlates`, `CveCascade`, `DatePlates` (+ "5 days" band), `Terminal` (typed lines, a cursor);
  - `VerdictChip`, `CalibrationTriangle` (lights FAIL×3/PASS×3), `GateChecklist`;
  - `LowerThird`, `Counter` (count-up), `BacktestSplit`, `PrecedentSeal`;
  - `CaptureClip` (`OffthreadVideo` with a subtle push-in), `IrisTransition`, `EndCard`, `Captions` (from `timing.json`).
- **Composition `HeirloomDemo`** 1920×1080@60.
  - Scenes S01–S10 from `video/timing.json`: per scene, the start/duration in frames, the VO text and the caption chunks.
  - Default durations are the target times above. A script `video/scripts/retime.mjs` reads `video/public/audio/vo/S0x.mp3` with ffprobe when present, sets each scene to its VO length + padding (0.4 s head, 0.6 s tail; S10 holds the end card 4 s) and regenerates the captions.
- **Audio support (optional):**
  - if `video/public/audio/vo/S01.mp3…S10.mp3` exist, place them at the scene starts;
  - if `music.mp3` exists, lay it underneath at −18 dB with ducking to −24 dB under VO;
  - if `sfx/*.mp3` exist, place them on cue (tick, stamp, whoosh, boom).
  - Render `HeirloomDemo-silent.mp4` always, plus `HeirloomDemo-mix.mp4` when audio is present.
- **Deliverables** in `~/video-out/`:
  - `master/HeirloomDemo-silent.mp4` (+ `-captions.mp4` burned in) and `master/HeirloomDemo.srt`;
  - `scenes/S01.mp4…S10.mp4` (each scene alone, silent);
  - `captures/*` and `broll/*`;
  - `stills/*.png` (keyframes for review);
  - `EDIT-GUIDE.md`: per-scene timecodes, which VO file goes where, the SFX cue list with timecodes, music levels, export settings for YouTube (1080p60, H.264 16–20 Mbps, AAC 320 kbps), the neatlogs slot instructions.

## Quality bar (both sessions)
- Render stills at the key moment of every scene and **Read them**. Write the critique in `video/NOTES.md` and fix it before the final render.
- Watch for: legibility at 1080p (no text <28 px except mono ids ≥22 px), safe margins (5%), consistent brass and ink, no jank, no empty frames, no clipped words, captions in sync.
- **Honesty:**
  - only text from the VO table and real data;
  - "candidate backports"; no exploitability claim; the exact Ubuntu claim sentence;
  - the neatlogs UI never faked.

- **Method (virtual time):** Playwright + Chromium, viewport 1920×1080. `page.clock.install()` before load; per frame, `page.clock.runFor(1000/60)`, set the scroll position, then screenshot (JPEG q=92) → `ffmpeg -framerate 60` → MP4 (CRF 14).
  - This gives perfectly smooth 60 fps even though the box renders WebGL slowly.
  - First verify that the fake clock drives Motion and three.js (two frames 1 s apart must differ). If it doesn't, use CDP `Emulation.setVirtualTimePolicy`.
  - Scroll with easing (in-out) between keyframe positions. Use a local `vite preview` of main's build with a `?capture=1` flag (disables Lenis and exposes `window.__scrollTo`) if needed. Also check that the result matches production.
- **Shots** (file names `~/video-out/captures/<ID>.mp4`):
  - **SH01** hero idle (3D movement turning), 8 s.
  - **SH02** hero → scroll to "Watch it work", 4 s.

  - **SH09** economics, 6 s.
  - **SH10** evidence locker, 6 s.
  - **SH11** finale, 9 s.
  - **SHM** mobile 390×844 at DSF 3 scrolling the hero and campaign, 8 s.
- **Cursor:** render a tasteful custom cursor (a bone-coloured dot with a ring) injected into the page, moving on eased paths. No OS cursor.
- **GitHub** (dark colour scheme, logged out):
  - **GH01** PR #13: title, verdict table, then a smooth scroll to the claims table, 10 s.
  - **GH02** issue #6: the question → the owner's answer comment, 9 s.

Record source URL and licence in `video/ASSETS.md`. Trim to the best 6–10 s and colour-match to ink/brass (ffmpeg `eq`/`curves`, slight desaturation).

## Motion design and assembly (session V-MO): Remotion
- **Project:** `video/` in the heirloom repo (Remotion 4, TS, React). Renders are git-ignored; outputs go to `~/video-out/`.
- **Data:** import `site/web/public/site.json` (or `src/data/site.json`) and read evals for every number. Terminal lines come from real files: the noble 87890 probe logs on the `artifacts` branch (`git show artifacts:matrix/b4-20261011/CVE-2026-87890/...`), and `docs/entire/checkpoint-pr13-*.txt`.
- **Components:**
  - `KineticTitle`, `BrassUnderline`, `GuillocheRing` (procedural; reuse the site's generator), `Hallmark`;
  - `DistroPlates`, `CveCascade`, `DatePlates` (+ "5 days" band), `Terminal` (typed lines, a cursor);
  - `VerdictChip`, `CalibrationTriangle` (lights FAIL×3/PASS×3), `GateChecklist`;
  - `LowerThird`, `Counter` (count-up), `BacktestSplit`, `PrecedentSeal`;
  - `CaptureClip` (`OffthreadVideo` with a subtle push-in), `IrisTransition`, `EndCard`, `Captions` (from `timing.json`).
- **Composition `HeirloomDemo`** 1920×1080@60.
  - Scenes S01–S10 from `video/timing.json`: per scene, the start/duration in frames, the VO text and the caption chunks.
  - Default durations are the target times above. A script `video/scripts/retime.mjs` reads `video/public/audio/vo/S0x.mp3` with ffprobe when present, sets each scene to its VO length + padding (0.4 s head, 0.6 s tail; S10 holds the end card 4 s) and regenerates the captions.

  - if `video/public/audio/vo/S01.mp3…S10.mp3` exist, place them at the scene starts;
  - if `music.mp3` exists, lay it underneath at −18 dB with ducking to −24 dB under VO;
  - if `sfx/*.mp3` exist, place them on cue (tick, stamp, whoosh, boom).
  - Render `HeirloomDemo-silent.mp4` always, plus `HeirloomDemo-mix.mp4` when audio is present.
- **Deliverables** in `~/video-out/`:
  - `master/HeirloomDemo-silent.mp4` (+ `-captions.mp4` burned in) and `master/HeirloomDemo.srt`;

  - `EDIT-GUIDE.md`: per-scene timecodes, which VO file goes where, the SFX cue list with timecodes, music levels, export settings for YouTube (1080p60, H.264 16–20 Mbps, AAC 320 kbps), the neatlogs slot instructions.

## Quality bar (both sessions)
- Render stills at the key moment of every scene and **Read them**. Write the critique in `video/NOTES.md` and fix it before the final render.
- Watch for: legibility at 1080p (no text <28 px except mono ids ≥22 px), safe margins (5%), consistent brass and ink, no jank, no empty frames, no clipped words, captions in sync.
- **Honesty:**
  - only text from the VO table and real data;
  - "candidate backports"; no exploitability claim; the exact Ubuntu claim sentence;
  - the neatlogs UI never faked.

lines: +// Guilloché line-work: the engine-turned engraving on watch dials and banknotes.
+// Pure path generators, shared by scripts/guilloche.mjs (static SVGs) and the page (inline SVG).
+/** One closed polar curve r(θ) = r + amp·sin(lobes·θ + phase), as an SVG path. */
+function polar(cx: number, cy: number, r: number, amp: number, lobes: number, phase: number, steps: number) {
+    const rr = r + amp * Math.sin(lobes * t + phase);
+ * A rosette: `copies` phase-shifted polar curves spread over one lobe, so they cross into the
+ * familiar moiré. Returns one path per copy (so each can be drawn in on its own).
+}: { cx?: number; cy?: number; r?: number; amp?: number; lobes?: number; copies?: number; steps?: number } = {}) {
+  // the copies are shifted across one full period of the sine, so they braid into the moiré
+  return Array.from({ length: copies }, (_, k) => polar(cx, cy, r, amp, lobes, (k / copies) * Math.PI * 2, steps));
+/** A band of `copies` phase-shifted sine waves across [0, width], centred on y. */
+}: { width?: number; y?: number; amp?: number; wavelength?: number; copies?: number; step?: number } = {}) {
+    for (let x = 0; x <= width; x += step) d += `${x ? 'L' : 'M'}${f(x)} ${f(y + amp * Math.sin((x / wavelength) * Math.PI * 2 + ph))}`;
+/** The hallmark "H": a slab-serif capital built from rectangles, centred in a 100×100 box. */
+/** The hallmark's ring: a rosette band between r 37 and 45 in the 100×100 box. */
+export const hallmarkRing = (copies = 6, steps = 240) => rosette({ r: 41, amp: 3.2, lobes: 18, copies, steps });

EDIT-GUIDE.md 13234 chars
# Heirloom demo film: edit guide

Generated by `video/scripts/edit-guide.mjs` from `video/timing.json` (**target lengths: no VO files yet**), `video/sfx-cues.json` and the site data.
Total: **2:45** (9900 frames at 60 fps, 1920×1080). Timecodes are `MM:SS:FF` at 60 fps.

## Files

| File | Size | Duration |
|---|---|---|


- `master/HeirloomDemo-silent.mp4`: H.264 High, yuv420p, Rec.709, CRF 14 (preset slow), no audio track. This is the picture-locked master for your mix.
- `master/HeirloomDemo-captions.mp4`: the same picture with burned-in captions (Geist 34 px, bone on a 70% ink pill). Use it for X/LinkedIn autoplay.
- `master/HeirloomDemo.srt`: the captions as a sidecar (upload it to YouTube instead of burning in).
- `scenes/S01.mp4…S10.mp4`: each scene alone (silent), cut on the scene boundaries below. The masters are these scenes concatenated (no re-encode).
- `stills/S01.png…`: one key frame per scene.

## Scenes and VO placement

Each VO line starts **0.4 s after its scene start**; scenes end 0.6 s after the line (S10 holds the end card for 4 s).

| Scene | Start | End | Length | VO file → place at | VO (exact text) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S01 End of life | 00:00:00 | 00:09:00 | 9.00 s | `S01.mp3` → 00:00:24 | On the seventh of April, Django four-point-two reached end of life. No more security fixes. |
| S02 Still shipped | 00:09:00 | 00:21:00 | 12.00 s | `S02.mp3` → 00:09:24 | But Debian thirteen and Ubuntu twenty-four-oh-four still ship it. Since then, Django has published nineteen security advisories — and not one official patch for four-point-two. |
| S03 The finding | 00:21:00 | 00:41:00 | 20.00 s | `S03.mp3` → 00:21:24 | On October first, Ubuntu shipped a backport for one of them. Five days later, Django said its original fix was incomplete. We took Ubuntu's source package, ran a test calibrated on Django's own fix commits… and the code path Django closed is still reachable in Ubuntu's build. |
| S04 Heirloom | 00:41:00 | 00:52:00 | 11.00 s | `S04.mp3` → 00:41:24 | That test was run by Heirloom — an agent that keeps end-of-life software patched, and proves which old versions are actually vulnerable. |
| S05 The method | 00:52:00 | 01:11:00 | 19.00 s | `S05.mp3` → 00:52:24 | Its first rule: never trust a test that hasn't failed. For each advisory, Heirloom writes its own test, proves it fails on Django's vulnerable code and passes on the fix… and only then asks the real question: is the old version affected? |
| S06 The campaign | 01:11:00 | 01:39:00 | 28.00 s | `S06.mp3` → 01:11:24 | Then we let it run the whole campaign: nineteen advisories, replayed in the order Django published them. Thirteen candidate backports — each one failing before the fix, and passing after. Where it couldn't prove something, it filed the evidence instead of guessing. And when a new fix amended one it had already backported, it stacked the follow-up on its own pull request. |
| S07 One question | 01:39:00 | 01:56:00 | 17.00 s | `S07.mp3` → 01:39:24 | Across the whole campaign, it asked me one question — a real judgement call about changing Django's behaviour. I answered once. It sealed the answer as a precedent, and the next case reused it without asking. |
## SFX cues

## Site changes (query-param guarded, inert in production)
- `?capture=1`: `useSmoothScroll` skips Lenis.
- `three-demo.html?shot=orbit|macro|speed`: scripted camera paths for the beauty renders (`MovementCanvas` `shot`
  prop), restarted at t = 0 by the capturer (`window.__shotRestart`). The demo page is dev-only (not in the build);
  R3D shots run against `vite --port 4401`.

## What I checked and fixed (2–4 frames read per shot)
- **pauseAt race** under load ("Cannot fast-forward to the past"; SH09, SH10 failed): retry with a doubling margin.
- **`page.waitForTimeout` stalls** with a faked clock (SH01/SH02/SH11 hung for minutes): node-side sleeps instead.
- **3D first frame**: while the page waits in real time, R3F queues frames faster than SwiftShader draws them, so the
  first captured frame waits ~90 s for the backlog; later frames cost ~0.9 s alone, 2–3 s with 6 parallel jobs. Just
  slow, not wrong.
- **SH06** overshot the pinned gear train (gears slid under the nav at the end): it now ends at the pin's end (13 800).
- **SH07** overshot (the sticky heading went under the nav): it now ends at 15 470.
- **CFO01**: a "Keep your access" sign-in prompt with a Cloudflare check covered the sheet; closed via its ×. The
  page fits the viewport, so it's an 8 s hold (it renders headless fine; light UI).
- **EOL01**: 4.2 is under "Show more unmaintained releases"; clicked, then scrolled to the 4.2 row. The site has no
  dark theme.
- **R3D**: `waitForSelector('html[data-ready]')` needs `state: 'attached'` (`<html>` counts as "hidden").
- SH03: the dial, tiles stamping in, the date reveals and the Oct 6 connector all animate; no blank frames.
- SH04: plates lock, then the "5 DAYS" band and the terminal FAIL×3 / PASS×3 / FAIL×3, then the claim.
- SH05: cursor → CVE-2026-6907 × Django 4.2.30 (FIX READY) → press → the certificate slides in; the calibration
  triangle's lights fill (FAIL×3, PASS×3, L FAIL×3 → FIX READY). The receipt chunk is pre-imported so it opens on the
  next frame.
- SHM: 390×844 @3x → 1170×2532 (portrait; the phone hero shows the poster, by design: no 3D under 768 px).
- GitHub: dark scheme logged out, 125 % (1536×864 CSS at DSF 1.25), no cookie banner seen (hidden by CSS if served).
  GH03/GH04/GH05 pages are short, so their scrolls clamp to the bottom; the target text is mid-frame throughout.
